subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Clostridium perfringens is often linked to food poisoning from:
options: Large quantities of meat or stews left to cool slowly
questions.explain: C. perfringens spores survive cooking and multiply when bulk-cooked meat dishes cool too slowly.

questions.q: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is needed in the diet primarily for:
options: Formation of collagen and wound healing
questions.explain: Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis, supporting connective tissue and wound healing.

questions.q: Which is essential for stabilising a foam such as whisked egg-white meringue?
options: Partially denatured protein trapping air in a network
questions.explain: Whisking partly denatures egg protein, which stabilises the trapped air bubbles forming a foam.

questions.q: Freezing preserves food by:
options: Lowering water activity and temperature so micro-organisms cannot multiply
questions.explain: Freezing makes water unavailable and lowers temperature so micro-organisms become dormant, not dead.

questions.q: Bacteria require which range of conditions to multiply most rapidly?
questions.explain: Bacteria multiply rapidly given warmth, moisture, nutrients and sufficient time.

questions.q: A kosher diet, following Jewish dietary law, prohibits:
options: Mixing meat and dairy in the same meal
questions.explain: Kosher rules forbid combining meat and dairy and prohibit certain foods such as pork and shellfish.

questions.q: Antioxidant nutrients such as vitamins A, C and E help the body by:
options: Neutralising free radicals and limiting cell damage
questions.explain: Antioxidants quench free radicals, reducing oxidative damage linked to chronic disease.

questions.q: A complete protein from a single plant source that supplies all essential amino acids is:
questions.explain: Soya is unusual among plant foods in supplying all the essential amino acids.

questions.q: Water activity (aw) below approximately which value generally inhibits microbial growth?
questions.explain: Most micro-organisms cannot grow when water activity falls below about 0.6, the basis of drying.

questions.q: Which best describes glycogen?
options: A storage polysaccharide of glucose found in the liver and muscles
questions.explain: Glycogen is the body's storage carbohydrate, a branched polymer of glucose units.

questions.q: The browning of toast surfaces and the dry crust of bread is mainly due to:
questions.explain: Dextrinisation is the breakdown of starch to dextrins by dry heat, giving a brown colour.

questions.q: Bacterial spores, such as those of Clostridium and Bacillus, are a hazard because they:
options: Can survive normal cooking temperatures and germinate later
questions.explain: Heat-resistant spores can survive cooking and germinate into active bacteria if food is mishandled.

questions.q: Pickling preserves food by:
options: Lowering the pH with acid such as vinegar
questions.explain: The acetic acid in vinegar lowers the pH below the range in which most spoilage bacteria grow.

questions.q: Which is a sensory factor affecting food choice?
options: The aroma, taste and texture of a dish
questions.explain: Sensory factors include appearance, aroma, flavour, texture and sound, which influence appeal.

questions.q: If energy intake consistently exceeds energy expenditure, the most likely outcome is:
questions.explain: A positive energy balance stores surplus energy as body fat, causing weight gain.

questions.q: On a food label, the 14 major allergens (such as nuts and milk) must be:
options: Emphasised, for example in bold, within the ingredients list
questions.explain: Law requires the 14 named allergens to be emphasised in the ingredients list so consumers can identify them.

questions.q: Which factor would increase an adult's basal metabolic rate?
options: A greater proportion of lean muscle mass
questions.explain: Lean muscle is metabolically active, so a higher muscle mass raises BMR.

questions.q: Non-starch polysaccharide (dietary fibre) is important in the diet mainly because it:
options: Is a high biological value protein
Is the body's main source of essential fatty acids
Aids the passage of food through the gut and prevents constipation
questions.explain: NSP adds bulk, holds water and promotes peristalsis, helping prevent constipation and bowel disease.

questions.q: Modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) extends shelf life mainly by:
options: Altering the gases around the food to slow spoilage
Heating the food in the pack
questions.explain: MAP changes the proportions of gases (e.g. reducing oxygen) to slow microbial and chemical spoilage.

questions.q: Buying locally produced, seasonal food can support sustainability mainly by:
options: Increasing the use of imported produce
Removing the need for any farming
Reducing food miles and associated transport emissions
questions.explain: Local seasonal food typically travels shorter distances, lowering transport emissions and supporting local producers.

questions.q: Lactose intolerance occurs because the person:
options: Lacks sufficient lactase enzyme to digest milk sugar
questions.explain: Without enough lactase, lactose is not digested, causing bloating and discomfort.

questions.q: Which type of fatty acid contains no carbon-to-carbon double bonds?
questions.explain: Saturated fatty acids have all carbon bonds filled with hydrogen and no double bonds.

questions.q: Which mineral is most associated with the prevention of iron-deficiency anaemia?
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; a deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.q: Which bonds link amino acids together within the primary structure of a protein?
questions.explain: Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds formed in a condensation reaction during protein synthesis.

questions.q: Which is a cultural or religious factor that may influence food choice?
options: A sudden change in market price
questions.explain: Religious and cultural beliefs, such as vegetarianism or fasting, strongly shape what people choose to eat.

questions.q: A diet persistently high in saturated fat and salt most strongly increases the risk of:
questions.explain: High saturated fat and salt raise blood cholesterol and pressure, key risk factors for CHD.

questions.q: Which raising agent works by producing carbon dioxide when it reacts with an acid and moisture?
questions.explain: Baking powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid that release CO2 to aerate mixtures.

questions.q: Salmonella food poisoning is most commonly associated with:
options: Raw or undercooked poultry and eggs
questions.explain: Salmonella is frequently linked to raw or undercooked poultry, eggs and their products.

questions.q: Vitamin C is described as enhancing iron absorption because it:
options: Binds iron so it cannot be absorbed
Converts non-haem iron into the more readily absorbed ferrous form
questions.explain: Vitamin C reduces non-haem iron to the ferrous form, which is absorbed more easily.

questions.q: By UK law, which information must legally appear on most pre-packed food labels?
options: A list of ingredients in descending order of weight
questions.explain: Ingredients must be listed by descending weight, alongside allergens, durability dates and other required details.
